name: NIST SP 800-61: Authentication & Brute Force Incident Response
containment_steps: Step 1: Identify offending Source IP and inspect authentication success ratio.
Step 2: Apply immediate temporary network firewall drop rule (iptables/ufw or Windows Firewall) to block offending IP.
Step 3: Force temporary session termination and password reset on targeted accounts if any successful login occurred.
Step 4: Verify Fail2Ban or rate-limiting daemon status on SSH/RDP daemon.
Step 5: Enforce public-key authentication or Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

name: NIST SP 800-61: Suspicious Script Execution & Defense Evasion
containment_steps: Step 1: Isolate host endpoint from local subnet to prevent lateral movement (maintain SOC agent connectivity).
Step 2: Terminate offending PowerShell process tree and record process GUID and parent PID.
Step 3: Base64 decode obfuscated payload string and extract C2 IP/domain IOCs.
Step 4: Check DNS / Proxy logs for beaconing requests to extracted C2 endpoints.
Step 5: Submit extracted binary or staging script to malware sandbox for behavioral analysis.

name: NIST SP 800-61: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation Incident Response
containment_steps: Step 1: Immediately revoke sudo / administrative privileges for the suspect account.
Step 2: Lock out suspect account (usermod -L <username> or Disable-ADAccount).
Step 3: Audit /etc/sudoers, /etc/sudoers.d, and setuid binaries for unauthorized tampering or backdoors.
Step 4: Inspect active user sessions (who, w, ps aux) and terminate rogue tty sessions.
Step 5: Review cron jobs (/etc/cron*, /var/spool/cron) and systemd services created within past 24 hours.

name: NIST SP 800-61: Ransomware & Inhibit System Recovery Containment
containment_steps: Step 1: IMMEDIATELY isolate host from network (unplug virtual NIC / disable network adapter).
Step 2: Kill parent process executing vssadmin/wmic/bcdedit.
Step 3: Snapshot memory (RAM capture) for volatile malware analysis.
Step 4: Verify immutable offline backups and cloud repository integrity.
Step 5: Initiate emergency enterprise SOC alert and threat hunt across all endpoints for matching process hash.

name: NIST SP 800-61: Web Application Exploit & Data Exfiltration
containment_steps: Step 1: Blacklist offending IP on edge WAF / Cloudflare / reverse proxy.
Step 2: Identify vulnerable URI parameter and deploy virtual patching rule on WAF.
Step 3: Audit database query logs to determine extent of unauthorized table access.
Step 4: If credentials or customer PII were compromised, trigger regulatory notification workflow.
Step 5: Rotate database service account credentials immediately.
